title: M5 third experiment: finite quotient and exact signature period
scope: Six frozen period-foundation targets; cardinality bound and full M5 remain separate obligations

spec.name: M5.Period.quotient_finite
spec.guidance: Install the local instance F.Monic.finite_adjoinRoot, then use Module.finite_of_finite (ZMod 2). This must include monic F = 1; do not require a nontrivial quotient. Return only tactic lines without a leading by. Preserve the exact target.

metadata.meaning: The quotient is finite for every monic binary polynomial.

spec.name: M5.Period.root_is_unit
spec.guidance: Map Polynomial.X_mul_divX_add F through AdjoinRoot.mk F. AdjoinRoot.mk_self gives zero and the constant term maps to one. Thus the image of -F.divX is an inverse of root F; construct IsUnit using that inverse or isUnit_iff_exists_inv. No monicity, squarefreeness or irreducibility is necessary. Return only tactic lines without a leading by. Preserve the exact target.

metadata.meaning: Constant coefficient one supplies an explicit inverse for the residue of X.

spec.name: M5.Period.cyclic_dvd_iff_root_pow
spec.statement: ∀ (F : M5.BinaryPolynomial) (N : ℕ), F ∣ M5.cyclicModulus N ↔ (AdjoinRoot.root F) ^ N = 1
spec.guidance: Use AdjoinRoot.mk_eq_zero after unfolding cyclicModulus, and map_add/map_pow/map_one/mk_X. The quotient is characteristic two: CharTwo.neg_eq or add_eq_zero_iff_eq_neg removes minus one. This includes N = 0 and F = 1. Return only tactic lines without a leading by. Preserve the exact target.

metadata.meaning: Polynomial cyclic divisibility equals a power identity in the full quotient ring.

spec.name: M5.Period.period_law
spec.statement: ∀ (F : M5.BinaryPolynomial), F.Monic → F.coeff 0 = 1 → 0 < M5.signaturePeriod F ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, F ∣ M5.cyclicModulus N ↔ M5.signaturePeriod F ∣ N
spec.guidance: Install a local Finite (AdjoinRoot F) instance using quotient_finite. root_is_unit and IsUnit.isOfFinOrder give positive order. The equivalence follows from cyclic_dvd_iff_root_pow and orderOf_dvd_iff_pow_eq_one. This proves period existence and the exact all-order divisibility law for repeated factors too. Return only tactic lines without a leading by. Preserve the exact target.

metadata.meaning: The period is positive and cyclic occurrence orders are exactly its multiples.

spec.name: M5.Period.period_one
spec.guidance: Apply period_law to F = 1 at N = 1. Since 1 divides cyclicModulus 1, the resulting natural-number divisibility into 1 proves period equals 1. Avoid requiring a nontrivial ring instance. Return only tactic lines without a leading by. Preserve the exact target.

metadata.meaning: The degenerate quotient case agrees with the original convention t(1) = 1.

spec.name: M5.Period.period_dvd_of_dvd
spec.statement: ∀ (F G : M5.BinaryPolynomial), F.Monic → F.coeff 0 = 1 → G.Monic → G.coeff 0 = 1 → F ∣ G → M5.signaturePeriod F ∣ M5.signaturePeriod G
spec.guidance: By period_law, G divides its own cyclic modulus at signaturePeriod G. Compose F | G with this divisibility, and apply the period_law equivalence for F. This is the T | E step used in the packing/lift proof. Return only tactic lines without a leading by. Preserve the exact target.

metadata.meaning: Signature inclusion makes periods divide, supplying T | E for G = gcd(a,b).
